text:
arjun: quick thread — thinking about expanding the onboarding validation surface for new models. current flow runs perf bench + smoke evals, but we keep hitting surprises in production (kv cache edge cases, tokenization mismatches). want to sketch a middle-ground: a lightweight behavioral validator that sits between smoke and full bench. thoughts?

sophia: +1. can you outline what the validator would check? latency spikes / tokenization diffs / reproducibility?

arjun: exactly. rough list: 1) tokenization parity against runtime tokenizer (diff ratios) 2) incremental kv cache replay test (simulate prefix reuse) 3) a 95th latency microbenchmark on typical prompt shapes 4) top-5 log-prob sanity on a small golden prompt set 5) binary compatibility marker (onnx/torch ops present)

leah: agree with those. question: do we run this in CI or as part of the onboarding pipeline in staging infra? staging infra gives better signal but costs more.

arjun: my thinking: run tokenization parity + log-prob sanity in CI (cheap), run kv replay + latency microbench in a lightweight staging runner that uses a small dedicated GPU pool (short window, ephemeral). binary compat can be static analysis on artifacts.

matt: for kv replay, we need a deterministic seed of cached KV shapes. how do we get that for new models without huge corpus? we could synthesize prefixes based on position/length distributions.

sophia: we already collect token length distribution from public prompt telemetry (anonymized). small synthetic generator could sample from that distribution. keep seeds in model-metadata.

arjun: prototype config idea (yaml):
```
validator:
  ci_checks:
    - tokenization_parity:
        sample_size: 2000
        max_diff_ratio: 0.01
    - logprob_sanity:
        prompts: /golden/prompts/short.jsonl
        topk_threshold: 0.02
  staging_checks:
    - kv_replay:
        prefixes: /model-metadata/kv-seeds.json
        max_latency_p95_ms: 120
    - latency_microbench:
        shapes: [short, med, long]
        p95_budget_ms: 200
  static_checks:
    - op_compatibility:
        allowed_missing_ops: []
```

leah: looks sensible. few tradeoffs: 1) tokenization_parity can fail for intentionally different tokenizers (custom tokenizers) — we should allow opt-out with a documented rationale. 2) p95 budgets must be per-class (tiny L16 vs Ls 70).

matt: +1 on opt-out. Also, op_compatibility should output a migration hint: e.g., fallback to an ONNX-export shim or require a specific runtime flag. Otherwise infra team gets tickets.

infra-bot: FYI: staging pool request template is available at /infra/pool-requests. default GPU flavor for validator-runner: A10G-small. request takes ~4h to provision during peak.

arjun: good note — maybe we should make the staging validator run on dedicated pre-warmed nodes (burst windows) to cut provisioning cost. or use cached warm instances allocated during business hours.

qa-jen: from QA side: include a small adversarial prompt set that triggers common hallucination patterns — we can run a few output-diff checks (e.g., length-to-entropy regression). also capture output-detokenization anomalies (we saw some models emit control bytes).

sophia: yes, add detokenization-safety check. cheap: run full decode on golden prompts and check for non-utf8 or control ranges.

arjun: final-ish proposal: - CI: tokenization parity, logprob sanity, detokenization safety - Staging: kv replay, latency microbench, adversarial-sanity - Static: op compatibility + export hints - Metadata: include generator seeds, tokenizer-id, recommended quant/profile

leah: rollout plan? start as opt-in for 2 weeks, measure false-positive rate. then make mandatory for new model admissions.

matt: metrics to collect: failure rates per-check, time-to-run, infra cost per-run, and post-admit incident correlation (did models that failed later cause regressions?).

arjun: action items: 1) i’ll put up a short RFC with config + metrics (this week) 2) sophia to draft tokenization parity tool contract 3) matt to prototype kv-seed generator 4) qa-jen to assemble golden + adversarial prompt sets

sophia: will do tokenization contract draft by EOD Friday.

matt: prototype by next Tue.

leah: i'll schedule the opt-in pilot and coordinate with infra to reserve burst pool windows.

infra-bot: note: if you tag @infra-eng I'll expedite the pool request review.

arjun: thanks all :thumbsup: keeping this small and iterative is the goal — want to catch these classes of failure earlier without full bench costs. ping me if you want to join the RFC review.

sophia: tagging @documents for RFC when ready.

qa-jen: adding a quick checklist for the QA run in the thread so it's visible: - golden short prompts run - adversarial suite run - detokenization check - basic output-stability (topk matches)

matt: one more thought — include a 'fuzzy-pass' for models that intentionally tweak tokenization: record divergence and require a compatibility shim at runtime. That preserves flexibility.

arjun: agreed — include 'compatibility_policy' in metadata: opt-in, strict, shim-required.

leah: cool. I'll collect these notes into the pilot onboarding doc and link when ready.

end of thread
